Title: Americans are living longer, but how does Mississippi rank? See where people live longest
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
Dec. 29, 2024, 4:12 a.m. CT
Good news! According to information from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Americans are living longer.
In 2023, the average life expectancy for Americans was 78.4. That's about a .9 increase compared to 2022. For men, it increased by a full year, and for women, the increase was just under a year.
Life expectancy at birth increased by almost a year because of improvements in the mortality rates from COVID, heart disease, cancer, diabetes and accidental injuries.
Average life expectancy at 65 also increased by more than 6 months for the total population.
About 189,000 fewer people died in 2023 compared to the previous year. The number of COVID-19 deaths dropped by 186,552 in 2022 to 49,932 last year.
See where Mississippi ranks in the U.S. and which counties have the longest and shortest life expectancies.

## How long do people live in Mississippi?
Mississippi ranked dead last in a CDC ranking of all 50 states and the District of Columbia when looking at 2021 data. The magnolia state had a 70.9-year life expectancy rate, slightly lower than West Virginia's 71.
The life expectancy for men in Mississippi was also 51st at 67.7 years.
Women, however, ranked 50th with an average of 74.3. West Virginia woman were in 51st place.
At age 65, people in Mississippi are expected to live about another 16 years, on average. It's about 14.6 years for men and 17.5 years for women.

## Where do people live the longest in Mississippi?
The University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute ranks life expectancies by county on itsCounty Health Rankings & Roadmaps site. Overall, it ranks Mississippi at 72.5.
The formula uses length and quality of life, paired with factors like health behavior, access to clinical care, the environment and social and economic factors to give counties a value for average life expectancy. (Issaquena was not given a value.)
Overall, the state ranks poorly on food environment, which prioritizes healthy options and food security. The state also has higher rates than the U.S. averages for sexually transmitted infections, teen pregnancy, physical inactivity, adult smoking and adult obesity.
Mississippi scored lower than national averages for excessive drinking and alcohol-related driving deaths.

## Where do people live the longest in Mississippi?
### Where do people live the longest in Mississippi?
The five counties with the longest life expectancies:
*   Lamar: 78.1  
*   Rankin: 77.4.  
*   Kemper: 76.5.  
*   Lafayette: 76.4.  
*   Greene: 76.1.

## Where do people live the longest in Mississippi?
### Where are the shortest life spans in Mississippi?
The counties with the shortest life expectancies:
*   Tunica: 65.4.  
*   Coahoma: 66.2.  
*   Neshoba: 66.9.  
*   Quitman: 67.  
*   Leflore: 67.1

## What are the 10 leading causes of death in the US?
The 10 leading causes of death stayed the same from 2022 to 2023, according to the CDC, but their order in the rankings shifted. Notably, COIVD-19 fell from the No. 4 spot in 2022 to No. 10 in 2023. The Top 3 stayed the same, and other causes moved up one spot compared to 2022.
1.   Heart disease.  
2.   Cancer.  
3.   Unintentional injuries.  
4.   Stroke.  
5.   Chronic lower respiratory diseases.  
6.   Alzheimer disease.  
7.   Diabetes.  
8.   Kidney disease.  
9.   Chronic liver disease and cirrhosis.  
10.   COVID-19.

## Which state has the longest life expectancy?
According to CDC data, Hawaii has the longest life expectancy is the U.S. at 79.9 years on average.
Four other states have life expectancies of at least 79 years, including Massachusetts, Connecticut, New York and New Jersey.

## What about neighboring states?
It's not looking great for the South. The states surrounding Mississippi have some of the lowest life expectancies in the CDC rankings. Arkansas ranked 45th, Tennessee ranked 46th, Louisiana ranked 48th, and Alabama was 49th.
Average life expectancies for each state were:
*   Alabama: 72.  
*   Arkansas: 72.5.  
*   Louisiana: 72.2.  
*   Tennessee: 72.4.

Title: Americans are living longer, but how does Mississippi rank? See where people live longest
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
Dec. 29, 2024, 4:12 a.m. CT
Good news! According to information from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Americans are living longer.
In 2023, the average life expectancy for Americans was 78.4. That's about a .9 increase compared to 2022. For men, it increased by a full year, and for women, the increase was just under a year.
Life expectancy at birth increased by almost a year because of improvements in the mortality rates from COVID, heart disease, cancer, diabetes and accidental injuries.
Average life expectancy at 65 also increased by more than 6 months for the total population.
About 189,000 fewer people died in 2023 compared to the previous year. The number of COVID-19 deaths dropped by 186,552 in 2022 to 49,932 last year.
See where Mississippi ranks in the U.S. and which counties have the longest and shortest life expectancies.

## How long do people live in Mississippi?
Mississippi ranked dead last in a CDC ranking of all 50 states and the District of Columbia when looking at 2021 data. The magnolia state had a 70.9-year life expectancy rate, slightly lower than West Virginia's 71.
The life expectancy for men in Mississippi was also 51st at 67.7 years.
Women, however, ranked 50th with an average of 74.3. West Virginia woman were in 51st place.
At age 65, people in Mississippi are expected to live about another 16 years, on average. It's about 14.6 years for men and 17.5 years for women.

## Where do people live the longest in Mississippi?
The University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute ranks life expectancies by county on itsCounty Health Rankings & Roadmaps site. Overall, it ranks Mississippi at 72.5.
The formula uses length and quality of life, paired with factors like health behavior, access to clinical care, the environment and social and economic factors to give counties a value for average life expectancy. (Issaquena was not given a value.)
Overall, the state ranks poorly on food environment, which prioritizes healthy options and food security. The state also has higher rates than the U.S. averages for sexually transmitted infections, teen pregnancy, physical inactivity, adult smoking and adult obesity.
Mississippi scored lower than national averages for excessive drinking and alcohol-related driving deaths.

## Where do people live the longest in Mississippi?
### Where do people live the longest in Mississippi?
The five counties with the longest life expectancies:
*   Lamar: 78.1  
*   Rankin: 77.4.  
*   Kemper: 76.5.  
*   Lafayette: 76.4.  
*   Greene: 76.1.

## Where do people live the longest in Mississippi?
### Where are the shortest life spans in Mississippi?
The counties with the shortest life expectancies:
*   Tunica: 65.4.  
*   Coahoma: 66.2.  
*   Neshoba: 66.9.  
*   Quitman: 67.  
*   Leflore: 67.1

## What are the 10 leading causes of death in the US?
The 10 leading causes of death stayed the same from 2022 to 2023, according to the CDC, but their order in the rankings shifted. Notably, COIVD-19 fell from the No. 4 spot in 2022 to No. 10 in 2023. The Top 3 stayed the same, and other causes moved up one spot compared to 2022.
1.   Heart disease.  
2.   Cancer.  
3.   Unintentional injuries.  
4.   Stroke.  
5.   Chronic lower respiratory diseases.  
6.   Alzheimer disease.  
7.   Diabetes.  
8.   Kidney disease.  
9.   Chronic liver disease and cirrhosis.  
10.   COVID-19.

## Which state has the longest life expectancy?
According to CDC data, Hawaii has the longest life expectancy is the U.S. at 79.9 years on average.
Four other states have life expectancies of at least 79 years, including Massachusetts, Connecticut, New York and New Jersey.

## What about neighboring states?
It's not looking great for the South. The states surrounding Mississippi have some of the lowest life expectancies in the CDC rankings. Arkansas ranked 45th, Tennessee ranked 46th, Louisiana ranked 48th, and Alabama was 49th.
Average life expectancies for each state were:
*   Alabama: 72.  
*   Arkansas: 72.5.  
*   Louisiana: 72.2.  
*   Tennessee: 72.4.

## Get the data story
Alabama’s fertility rate of 59.1 births per 1,000 women ages 15-44 ranks 22 nd among states in the U.S. and is lower than the national fertility rate of 60.1. Alabama ranks 10 th in teen birth rates, 6 th in births to unmarried mothers, and 3 rd in low birthweight and preterm births. The infant mortality rate in Alabama is 7 infant deaths per 1,000 live births, tied for 7 th highest in the U.S. Alabama has the 2 nd highest firearm death rate in the nation – 21.8 firearm deaths per 100,000 – and the 3 rd highest homicide rate at 12.2 homicides per 100,000. However, Alabama’s death rate from drug overdoses ranks 32 nd among states and is nearly 25% lower than the national overdose death rate. Heart Disease is the leading cause of death in Alabama, followed by: (2) Cancer (3) Chronic Lung Disease (4) Stroke (5) Accidents (6) Alzheimer Disease (7) Influenza/Pneumonia (8) Diabetes (9) Kidney Disease, and (10) Septicemia. The marriage rate in Alabama of 6.8 marriages per 1,000 is slightly higher than the national rate, and the divorce rate in the state of 3.7 divorces per 1,000 is over 24% higher than the rate for the entire United States.

# Stats of the States: Alabama
## Get the data story
Alabama’s fertility rate of 59.1 births per 1,000 women ages 15-44 ranks 22 nd among states in the U.S. and is lower than the national fertility rate of 60.1. Alabama ranks 10 th in teen birth rates, 6 th in births to unmarried mothers, and 3 rd in low birthweight and preterm births. The infant mortality rate in Alabama is 7 infant deaths per 1,000 live births, tied for 7 th highest in the U.S. Alabama has the 2 nd highest firearm death rate in the nation – 21.8 firearm deaths per 100,000 – and the 3 rd highest homicide rate at 12.2 homicides per 100,000. However, Alabama’s death rate from drug overdoses ranks 32 nd among states and is nearly 25% lower than the national overdose death rate. Heart Disease is the leading cause of death in Alabama, followed by: (2) Cancer (3) Chronic Lung Disease (4) Stroke (5) Accidents (6) Alzheimer Disease (7) Influenza/Pneumonia (8) Diabetes (9) Kidney Disease, and (10) Septicemia. The marriage rate in Alabama of 6.8 marriages per 1,000 is slightly higher than the national rate, and the divorce rate in the state of 3.7 divorces per 1,000 is over 24% higher than the rate for the entire United States.
SOURCE: National Vital Statistics System, 2018
LINK: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/state-stats/states/al.html

# Stats of the States: Arkansas
## Get the data story
Arkansas has the highest teen birth rate in the nation (30.4 live births per 1,000 females ages 15-19), and the 10 th highest overall fertility rate for women of all ages. Arkansas also has the 3 rd highest marriage rate in the country, behind Nevada and Hawaii, but also the 2 nd highest divorce rate (behind Nevada). The leading cause of death in the state is Heart Disease, followed by (2) Cancer (3) Chronic Lower Respiratory Disease (4) Stroke (5) Accidents (6) Alzheimer disease (7) Diabetes (8) Kidney Disease (9) Influenza & Pneumonia, and (10) Suicide. The infant mortality rate in Arkansas is the 3 rd highest in the country. The state ranks 6 th in cesarean deliveries and in low birthweight births and 5 th in preterm births. However, the drug overdose rate in Arkansas of 15.7 overdose deaths per 100,000 people is among the lower rates in the country and is 27% lower than the national rate.
SOURCE: National Vital Statistics System, 2018

# Stats of the States: Arkansas
## Get the data story
Arkansas has the highest teen birth rate in the nation (30.4 live births per 1,000 females ages 15-19), and the 10 th highest overall fertility rate for women of all ages. Arkansas also has the 3 rd highest marriage rate in the country, behind Nevada and Hawaii, but also the 2 nd highest divorce rate (behind Nevada). The leading cause of death in the state is Heart Disease, followed by (2) Cancer (3) Chronic Lower Respiratory Disease (4) Stroke (5) Accidents (6) Alzheimer disease (7) Diabetes (8) Kidney Disease (9) Influenza & Pneumonia, and (10) Suicide. The infant mortality rate in Arkansas is the 3 rd highest in the country. The state ranks 6 th in cesarean deliveries and in low birthweight births and 5 th in preterm births. However, the drug overdose rate in Arkansas of 15.7 overdose deaths per 100,000 people is among the lower rates in the country and is 27% lower than the national rate.
SOURCE: National Vital Statistics System, 2018
LINK: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/state-stats/states/ar.html

## How have the leading causes of death changed over time?
Here’s how death rates changed from 1999 to 2024:
*   Heart disease decreased by 12%  
*   Cancer remained relatively stable  
*   Accidents increased by 66%  
*   Cerebrovascular disease decreased by 31%  
*   Chronic respiratory illness increased by 30%
COVID-19 became one of the leading causes at the onset of the pandemic, but its rank has since dropped off.
Cancer and heart disease are consistently the leading causes of death.
